output:
I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data.

That call was malformed and didn't run. I'll check the environment and the rest of the checker before writing the script.

The script is at `/app/bin/payroll.py`, and its result for `/app/data` is saved in `/app/out/payroll.json`. `python3 tools/check_payroll.py` printed "OK: every value matches the approved figures." All 150 employees match on every field. The exception counts and totals match too.

I wrote it from the rules in the three docs rather than from this period's files. Only the standard library is used, and it handles all seven export formats, including gzip files and header changes partway through a file.

A few cases in the rules aren't covered by this period's data, so I made my own choices:
- **No rate on or before a shift's workday:** the script uses the employee's earliest rate. The rules don't say what to do here.
- **Same punch delivered twice:** the first copy it reads is kept. If a later copy disagreed, the later one would be ignored.
- **`add` correction for an unknown site:** the script ignores it, since there's no time zone to apply.

I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app; find . -type f | grep -v '^./.git/' | head -100; cat docs/payroll-rules.md docs/exports.md docs/output.md

cd /app; ls data data/corrections | head -30; ls data/exports; cat data/sites.csv data/period.json; head -5 data/employees.csv data/rates.csv; cat tools/check_payroll.py | head -60; head -c 600 tools/reference-digests.json; ls /app /app/bin /app/out; git status 2>&1 | head -3

cd /app/data; for s in exports/*; do echo "=== $s"; ls $s | wc -l; ls $s | head -3; f=$(ls $s/* | head -1); head -c 500 $f; echo; done; head -5 corrections/batch-1.csv; file exports/*/* | grep -vi 'text' | head; for f in exports/*/*; do head -c2 $f | xxd -p | grep -q 1f8b && echo gz $f; done | head
cd /app; python3 bin/payroll.py data out/payroll.json && python3 tools/check_payroll.py; head -c 600 out/payroll.json

cd /app; echo '{"status":"success","summary":"Wrote /app/bin/payroll.py (stdlib only) implementing the documented formats and rules, ran it on /app/data to /app/out/payroll.json; tools/check_payroll.py reports every value matching the approved figures."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
